title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 356 (Power of Tribunal to declare dissolution of company void)

content.overview: Where a company has been dissolved, the Tribunal may at any time within two years of the date of the dissolution, on application by the liquidator of the company or by any other person who appears to the Tribunal to be interested, make an order, upon such terms as the Tribunal thinks fit, declaring the dissolution to have been void, and thereupon such proceedings may be taken as might have been taken if the company had not been dissolved.
content.glance: Within two years of dissolution, Tribunal may on application declare the dissolution void; proceedings may then continue as if the company had not been dissolved.
content.study: Section 356 allows the Tribunal to resurrect a dissolved company for limited purposes. Within two years of the dissolution date, on application by the liquidator or any other person who appears to the Tribunal to be interested, the Tribunal may order that the dissolution is void, on such terms as it thinks fit. Once the order is made, proceedings may be taken as if the company had not been dissolved.

sections.heading: Voiding dissolution

examples.title: Overlooked asset
examples.body: After dissolution an undiscovered bank account is found. Within two years the former liquidator applies under s. 356; the Tribunal declares the dissolution void so that the asset can be recovered and distributed.

hypotheticals.question: Is there a time limit for an application under s. 356?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes. The application must be made within two years of the date of the dissolution.
